blocks.content: This chapter covers Delhi-specific flagship schemes across successive governments and the most recent (2025-26) policy developments under the current BJP government - a fast-changing, high-value current-affairs chapter that candidates should re-verify close to their exam date.
Legacy Flagship Schemes (2015-2025, AAP Government Era)

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Legacy Flagship Schemes cover the AAP Government Era from 2015 to 2025.
Recent Developments detail government policy initiatives for the 2025-26 period.
Central Government Schemes maintain a significant presence in the Delhi region.

cells: Subsidised electricity (up to a monthly consumption threshold) and free water supply (up to a monthly limit) for Delhi households, a hallmark AAP-era welfare policy
Neighbourhood-level primary healthcare clinics offering free consultations, medicines and diagnostic tests, aimed at decongesting larger hospitals
Major investment in government school infrastructure and pedagogy, including the 'Happiness Curriculum' and Entrepreneurship Mindset Curriculum
Free DTC/cluster bus travel scheme for women passengers across Delhi

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: These AAP-era schemes remain relevant exam material even after the 2025 change of government, since they defined Delhi's welfare-policy identity for a decade and are frequently referenced in comparative/before-after policy questions.
Recent Developments Under the Current Government (2025-26)

items: Following the BJP's February 2025 Assembly win, the Rekha Gupta government has emphasised infrastructure delivery, civic-services improvement, and continuation of certain welfare schemes alongside new initiatives, with regular joint LG-CM reviews of city administration (e.g., the 2026 heatwave action plan review) signalling closer coordination between the LG and the elected government than in the preceding decade.

A large-scale, coordinated heat-relief plan was implemented across all 13 districts of Delhi in 2026 (following a call from the Prime Minister the previous year), including mobile relief units distributing free water, ORS packets, and shade/cooling assistance during peak summer heatwaves.

Continued emphasis on the Yamuna cleanup and stricter GRAP enforcement has featured prominently in the current government's public communications, alongside efforts to accelerate stalled infrastructure and urban-development projects.

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Questions on 'recent Delhi government initiatives' are best answered with the general THEME (heatwave response, Yamuna cleanup, GRAP enforcement, civic-infrastructure push) rather than memorised specifics, since exact scheme names and dates change rapidly under any government - always cross-check the latest news closer to your exam.
Central Government Schemes with a Strong Delhi Presence

items: Distinguish between legacy schemes from the 2015-2025 AAP Era and developments in 2025-26.
Focus on Central Government initiatives specifically implemented or active within Delhi.

As the national capital, Delhi is the headquarters location for the administration of virtually all pan-India central schemes (Ayushman Bharat, PM Awas Yojana, Swachh Bharat Mission, etc.), though the NCT government has, at various points, opted in or out of specific central schemes depending on the political alignment between the Centre and the Delhi government of the day.

Delhi hosts major central government institutions relevant to governance/administration exams generally - the Election Commission of India, NITI Aayog, UPSC, and most central ministries - making it India's de facto administrative nerve-centre beyond its own NCT-specific governance.
AAP-era (2015-2025) flagship schemes: free electricity/water subsidy, Mohalla Clinics, Happiness Curriculum, free bus travel for women.
2025-26: BJP government under CM Rekha Gupta emphasises infrastructure delivery and closer LG-CM coordination.
2026 heatwave action plan implemented across all 13 Delhi districts, including mobile relief units.
Delhi hosts most central government ministries, the Election Commission of India, NITI Aayog, and UPSC - India's administrative nerve-centre.
